title: Welcome to the marry month of June
primary_topics: Personal narrative of the Panganibans' Diamond (60th) Wedding Anniversary on April 8, 2021 -- originally planned at the Vatican or Manila Cathedral, ultimately commemorated via online Mass after the enhanced community quarantine restricted travel and religious services
Three advices for couples, drawn from 60 years of marriage and delivered extemporaneously after the anniversary Mass
Closing reflection on God's mysterious providence and the unexpected blessing of long-deferred 'kumustahan' with relatives
Welcoming readers to 'the marry month of June' through a personal devotional-romantic essay
sub_topics: Original wedding date: April 8, 1961, at the Immaculate Conception Church (now Cathedral) in Cubao, Quezon City

Online Eucharistic Celebration presided over by 'adopted anak' Msgr. Gerry O. Santos from his Sts. Peter and Paul parish in Makati, with family joining from the Philippines, US, Canada, UK, and Australia
Backstory: Msgr. Santos first met in the mid-1980s as a new priest; catechized and taught the author Catholic theology; mutual 'Tay/'Nay/Anak terms of endearment

Advice 1 -- 'Talk it over': two unbendable rules ('My wife is always right' / 'Always follow the first rule'); Leni's affectionate reply that she trusts her husband's judgment ('If you can pass final judgments on persons accused of murder, rape, kidnapping...'); when serious disputes arise, talk again and again until a solution emerges

Advice 2 -- 'Pray together every evening': hold hands, extemporized prayer in English or Tagalog; thanksgiving for the day's work and intercession for tomorrow's chores; quarrels never last more than a day
Advice 3 -- 'Trust the Lord always': sometimes God seems not to answer; remembering 'My thoughts are not your thoughts and My ways are not your ways' (Isaiah)

Cardinal Chito Tagle had already reserved the original April 8 date at the Vatican; the Manila Cathedral was the 'Plan B' venue (Ambassador Tita de Villa's affectionate description of its symbolic resonance)
Severe ECQ imposed March 29 - April 11 restricted international travel and local religious services, forcing the online pivot
Big unexpected blessing: 'kumustahan' with relatives not seen in a long time; agreement to do online reunion again every January 1 at 10 a.m. Manila time
Pointer to the full speech text at cjpanganiban.com

stances.claim: Sustained marriage rests on three habits: talk it over (until a solution comes); pray together every evening (extemporized in English or Tagalog, holding hands); and trust the Lord always (especially when God seems not to answer).
stances.evidence: 60 years of personal marital experience; specific household practices described

stances.claim: Serious-dispute resolution requires repeated honest conversation supplemented by consultation with family elders, priests, and trusted friends — and when no solution comes, talking again and again until one does.
stances.evidence: The Panganibans' own experience and process

stances.claim: Daily evening prayer prevents quarrels from outlasting the day and dissolves accumulated stress, depression, and sulking — a habit rather than a memorized devotion.

Trusting the Lord even amid disappointment reframes broken plans as unexpected blessings — the cancelled Vatican / Manila Cathedral ceremony became an unexpected family reunion via Zoom, prompting an agreed annual January 1 online reunion.
stances.evidence: ECQ-forced pivot; family reunion outcome; commitment to recurring online reunion

notable_anecdotes: 60-year marital tradition reduced to two 'unbendable rules': 'My wife is always right' and 'Always follow the first rule' — paired with Leni's affectionate retort that 'if you can pass final judgments on persons accused of murder, rape, kidnapping, and other despicable crimes, I think I can trust you.'

The pandemic-collapsed plans: Cardinal Chito Tagle had already reserved April 8 in his calendar for a Vatican ceremony; prospective ninongs and ninangs had agreed to fly to Rome; Ambassador Tita de Villa's lyrical Plan-B description of the Manila Cathedral as 'symbolic of the love needed by marriage to be restored to its original beauty.'

Msgr. Gerry O. Santos as 'adopted anak,' first met in the mid-1980s as a new priest, presiding via Zoom from Sts. Peter and Paul parish in Makati, with relatives joining from the Philippines, US, Canada, UK, and Australia — and the author's quiet realization 'until the headcount how international our family had become.'

The unexpected blessing of the cancellation: a long-overdue 'kumustahan' with relatives not seen in a long, long time — and an agreement to do online reunions again every January 1 at 10 a.m. Manila time.
The Isaiah citation 'My thoughts are not your thoughts and My ways are not your ways' as the operative scriptural anchor of the 'Trust the Lord always' advice.

one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban opens this Sunday devotional-romantic column with the announcement that he and his wife Leni had hoped to celebrate their Diamond Wedding Anniversary on April 8 -- 60 years after their April 8, 1961 wedding at the Immaculate Conception Church (now Cathedral) in Cubao -- at the Vatican (Cardinal Chito Tagle had already reserved the date and prospective ninongs and ninangs had agreed to fly to Rome) or at the Manila Cathedral (Ambassador Tita de Villa's lyrical 'Plan B' venue, 'symbolic of the love needed by marriage to be restored to its original beauty'). The March 29 - April 11 enhanced community quarantine collapsed both plans, so the blessed day was commemorated by a simple online Mass presided over via Zoom by their 'adopted anak,' Msgr. Gerry O. Santos, from his Sts. Peter and Paul parish in Makati -- with close relatives joining from the Philippines, United States, Canada, United Kingdom, and Australia, prompting the author's quiet realization 'until the headcount how international our family had become.' To welcome lovers and couples to 'the marry month of June,' he shares his three extemporaneous advices delivered after the Mass: (1) 'Talk it over' -- anchored by two playful 'unbendable rules' ('My wife is always right. And the second: Always follow the first rule'), Leni's affectionate retort ('If you can pass final judgments on persons accused of murder, rape, kidnapping, and other despicable crimes, I think I can trust you'), and the iterative practice of talking again and again, with elder/priest/trusted-friend consultation, until a solution emerges; (2) 'Pray together every evening' -- extemporized in English or Tagalog while holding hands, thanking the Lord for the day's work and asking for the next morning's chores, never letting a quarrel last more than a day; and (3) 'Trust the Lord always' -- anchored by the Isaiah refrain 'My thoughts are not your thoughts and My ways are not your ways,' which reframed the cancelled Vatican/Manila Cathedral plans as the unexpected blessing of a long-overdue 'kumustahan' with relatives not seen in a long time. The couple agreed to do the online reunion again every January 1 at 10 a.m. Manila time.
